initial_prompts: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: production 2D fighting-game transparent sprite atlas. The two input images are CHARACTER/STYLE REFERENCES. Preserve Sonic Tusk exactly: squat muscular purple-gray humanoid sound monster, one head, huge paired ivory curled horns with metallic purple-ringed tips beside his face, two long downward ivory mouth tusks, small glowing purple eyes, big black speaker housings on both shoulders/back, black metallic gauntlets and heavy boots with purple circular details, brown ragged loincloth and black belt with round purple jewel. Match the existing shaded inked comic sprite look and proportions. Fixed left-facing three-quarter view, complete whole bodies, same camera and scale in every cell, attached limbs, no redesign. Create one NEW square 4-column by 4-row atlas containing exactly sixteen poses. Each sprite must be centered in its own equal cell with at least 12% transparent margin on every side; no touching or overlap with neighboring figures. Standing bodies fill about 70% of each cell height. Actual transparent background, no ground shadow, no background color, no effects, no projectiles, no circles, no labels, no lettering or grid. Keep natural shaded materials and sharp clean alpha edges. Preserve all horns, speakers, hands and feet fully inside their cell. This is the locomotion/reaction sheet. Strict row-major ordering: poses 0-7 form ONE continuous eight-frame walk toward screen left, with alternating legs and counter-swinging arms: 0 left foot forward contact; 1 weight/down on left foot; 2 right foot passing the planted left; 3 right foot moving forward, left pushing off; 4 right foot forward contact; 5 weight/down on right foot; 6 left foot passing the planted right; 7 left foot moving forward toward next contact. Keep his heavy grounded weight; use distinct actual leg positions, not eight copies of idle. Poses 8-11: four consecutive subtle breathing idle stances, feet fixed and fists ready, chest rises then settles. Pose 12: light punch recoil, chest/head rocked backward, feet planted. Pose 13: strong kick recoil, torso pushed backward and arms raised. Pose 14: stagger with rear leg catching balance. Pose 15: deliberate return to guard. No airborne walking poses. Sixteen separate whole-body drawings, no missing cells.

opposite_step_prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a production sprite atlas with FOUR new full-body walking keyframes of Sonic Tusk, arranged TWO columns by TWO rows on a genuinely transparent background. The provided image is a CHARACTER AND STYLE REFERENCE. Match exactly the same one-headed muscular purple-gray monster, giant curled ivory horns with black/purple metal tips, two downward mouth tusks, shoulder/back speakers, black gauntlets and boots with violet jewel details, brown loincloth, and shaded inked comic rendering. Same left-facing three-quarter camera and proportions. No added heads, limbs, equipment, labels, grid, shadows, effects or colors outside the clean silhouette. Fixed scale, generous transparent margins, each whole body completely inside its cell.

These four drawings are specifically the MISSING OPPOSITE-LEG HALF of his walk. In the reference the LARGE NEAR-SIDE LEG keeps kicking toward SCREEN LEFT; DO NOT repeat that pose. For these new drawings, the LARGE NEAR-SIDE LEG MUST MOVE BACK toward SCREEN RIGHT and the OTHER SMALLER FAR-SIDE LEG steps FORWARD toward SCREEN LEFT. The near-side leg visibly exposes its shin and heel as it trails behind the hip. Keep the upper body oriented toward screen left. Do not mirror the whole character.

Row-major poses:
0: FAR-SIDE boot makes forward contact on screen LEFT; NEAR-SIDE boot trails far behind on screen RIGHT, heel raised. A clearly wide stride with the opposite leg leading from the reference.
1: weight settles onto the FAR-SIDE leftward boot, bent knee; NEAR-SIDE rightward trailing foot begins lifting off.
2: NEAR-SIDE trailing knee and boot pass UNDER the hips from the right while the FAR-SIDE boot stays planted on screen LEFT.
3: NEAR-SIDE knee moves forward toward screen LEFT to begin the next step; FAR-SIDE leg pushes off and extends toward SCREEN RIGHT.
Only TWO rows, TWO columns, FOUR unique poses. The leg identity/weight transfer is the crucial correction. No repeated forward-kick pose.
